articles.title: Half a million trees to be planted in England in three years, says government
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Environment secretary Angela Eagle to make pledge as part of efforts to protect against extreme weather

Half a million trees will be planted across England in the next three years…

blocks.text: Half a million trees will be planted across England in the next three years to protect against extreme weather, the environment secretary, Angela Eagle, will pledge on Wednesday morning.

Mayors, local authorities, charities and grassroots groups will be given new funding and responsibilities for restoring natural landscapes such as wetlands, river edges and meadows, which can provide natural flood management and reduce the damage done by droughts.
The £79m package, to be set out in Eagle’s speech to the Labour party conference in Liverpool, will include £53m for tree-planting and £26m for “local nature recovery strategies”.

This summer’s drought showed the urgent need for more trees, and more protection of natural landscapes, Eagle is to say. “In areas where nature has been allowed to flourish, the ground held more water, and the droughts were less severe,” she will tell the conference. “On streets where trees have been planted, the shade meant temperatures were lower. And when rain finally came, those same trees reduced the risk of floods. We all deserve access to the benefits that nature can bring.”

Trees can reduce air temperatures by 4C in cities, making heatwaves more bearable, while a single mature tree can intercept 15,000 litres of water a year, reducing flood and water run-off risks during storms. They can also halve noise pollution and absorb air pollution, and provide habitats for wildlife in towns and cities.

Echoing the localism agenda championed by Andy Burnham, Eagle will tell the Labour party conference the UK must combine a focus on local communities with the need to make the whole country more resilient to the increasingly intense impacts of the global climate crisis.
She will say that putting decision-making in the hands of those who know their communities best is the most effective way to improve nature and strengthen the UK against a changing climate.
Craig Bennett, the chief executive of The Wildlife Trusts, said the plans were “very encouraging”, and appeared to signal that Burnham would change the government’s direction on nature.

“The mood could not be more different from Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves, who presented nature as a block to development,” he said. “This will be very welcome. For a long time local authorities have been trying to help nature but did not have the power, money or political support. The Burnham government seems to have realised that nature is crucial to the country’s future.”
England has lost more than 90% of its wetlands over the last century. “We need to make Britain wet again,” said Bennett. “We could have tens of thousands of new wetlands.”

Richard Benwell, the chief executive of the Wildlife and Countryside Link charity, said: “Investing in the critical nature infrastructure we need to protect businesses and communities makes good economic sense and good ecological sense, especially when investments are guided by locally agreed nature restoration plans. This is a good start towards Burnham’s promise of the government getting ahead of long-term challenges, recognising nature’s role in supporting our economy and adapting to climate change.
“This should be followed by a commitment to rapidly scale up nature investment as part of the prime minister’s 10-year plan, funded by businesses who will benefit, and by making sure polluters pay.”

The government has faced sharp criticism in recent days over the management of payments to farmers, intended to help them protect nature on their land. Last Tuesday, the Sustainable Farming Incentive was opened at 10am for applications from farmers willing to undertake environmental improvements such as conserving wildlife habitats, growing trees and nurturing soil.
But within six hours, the £253m pot was exhausted and many farmers were left disappointed.

Bennett said farmers needed support to play their role in nature protection and fostering resilience to the climate crisis. “We need to stop thinking about this as just a farming budget, but as a national security and natural resilience budget,” he said.

articles.title: Malaysia begins Myanmar repatriations despite warnings from UN and rights groups
articles.summary:
Kuala Lumpur plans to send a total of 5,000 Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country despite persecution concerns

Malaysia began sending back about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday,…

blocks.text: Malaysia began sending back about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, the government confirmed, as it launched a scheme that rights groups say may endanger migrants and asylum seekers by returning them to the war-torn country.
The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar citizens that Kuala Lumpur says agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres amid a huge uptick in anti-migrant sentiment in Malaysia.
Both the UN and advocacy organisations voiced concern on Tuesday, saying the group could face a dangerous homecoming in Myanmar, where a civil war has raged since 2021.

Neither Malaysia nor Myanmar have officially clarified the number of Rohingya people in the first group, and there is worry they may be returned to a country where they face persecution rights groups say amounts to genocide. The Rohingya, a Muslim minority group, make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the UN.
Many of the Rohingya escaped to Malaysia during a brutal military crackdown in 2017.

On Tuesday afternoon, AFP reporters saw three ships belonging to the Myanmar navy, used in a previous repatriation exercise, departing from Malaysia’s Lumut naval base. The Myanmar nationals were processed at the naval base before boarding dozens of buses which arrived under police escort at the Majlis Perbandaran Manjung stadium.
Malaysia’s interior ministry confirmed that the repatriations were under way.

blocks.caption: A policeman walks in front of buses carrying Myanmar nationals being repatriated from Malaysia. Photograph: Arif Kartono/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: It said it a statement that the repatriation was part of the government’s plan to resolve the “legacy issue” of foreign asylum-seekers in Malaysia – of which it said 95% were from Myanmar.

“This long-standing issue has imposed a significant financial burden on the nation, triggered serious social crises, and created tangible security threats for the Malaysian people,” the statement said.
But in Geneva, the UN rights chief, Volker Turk, urged Malaysia to stop the process immediately, saying nobody should be deported to Myanmar, given the severity of the situation on the ground.

“This is no time to return anyone forcibly to a country plagued by egregious human rights violations and abuses, and where many cruelly face the real risk of more of the same violence again upon their return,” he said in a statement.
“The conditions are far from safe and sustainable, and it is deeply questionable whether any return in these circumstances can be considered truly voluntary.
“The hundreds of thousands who have fled Myanmar in fear for their lives must be protected, and their fundamental human rights to seek asylum and protection abroad properly considered.”

The Malaysian prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, announced in July that Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya. The plan was announced after authorities detained more than 100 Rohingya who had gathered outside the UN refugee agency’s office in Kuala Lumpur.
They were seeking help after being threatened with eviction from an informal settlement in northern Penang state. They were later released after officials confirmed they held valid UN documentation.
Myanmar earlier this month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad, after criticism from the UN and rights groups.

Last week more than 160 civil society groups in a joint statement called upon the Malaysian government to “immediately halt the deportations,” pending talks with civil organisations about the situation on the ground in Myanmar.
Malaysia, which shelters one of Southeast Asia’s biggest refugee populations, is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and does not formally recognise refugee status.

articles.title: World’s seas heated by a record 23 zettajoules last year
articles.summary:
The injection of thermal energy, 40 times that used by humanity in total, comes amid an increasing rise in sea levels and continuing acidification

A record-breaking 23 zettajoules of heat…

blocks.text: A record-breaking 23 zettajoules of heat was sunk into the world’s seas last year, leaving ocean waters hotter, higher and less hospitable, a report has found.

The explosive addition of thermal energy, which was almost 40 times greater than all the energy humanity used that year, comes amid far-reaching changes to the deep water bodies fundamental to life on Earth.

Sea levels have risen by about 3.8mm per year since 1999, and at a faster rate of 4.2mm per year between 2012 and 2025, according to the 10th edition of the Copernicus ocean state report. It found the global ocean has become 17% more acidic in the last 40 years.
Oceans have absorbed about one-third of the carbon dioxide that humanity has spewed and about 90% of the extra heat that greenhouse gas pollution has trapped in the Earth’s system.

“The ocean is transforming before our eyes,” said Pierre Bahurel, director general of Mercator Ocean International, which published the report. “Warming, rising seas and ecosystem degradation are interconnected signs of significant and long-term change.”

In Europe, which is heating twice as fast as the global average, the Mediterranean and Black Seas have been plagued by record-breaking marine heatwaves – with elevated temperatures that persist deep below the surface – and bouts of extreme heat that have lasted more than a month, the scientists found.

blocks.caption: A Mediterranean swimmer in mid-January: the entire sea has warmed by .32C per decade. Photograph: Hassan Ammar/AP

blocks.text: The scientists found a clear acceleration of sea level rise in the western Mediterranean, even as the eastern part showed uneven gains. The entire sea has warmed by 0.32C per decade, the report found, driving up marine heatwaves, particularly in the last few years.

The report comes as western Europe experiences an unusually warm September right after its ruinously fiery summer, with temperatures hitting 40C highs in parts of Spain and Portugal last week. Hot coastal waters exacerbate heatwaves on land by adding heat during nights that would otherwise cool down.
Ángel Borja, a marine ecologist at AZTI, a Basque research institute, who was not involved in the report, said the effects have already been seen for several years and will certainly increase.

“But it seems to be a problem that society tends to downplay. For example, the combined problems of rising sea levels and extreme events, which are eroding the Mediterranean coast – and yet some people insist on rebuilding in places that will undoubtedly disappear.”

The report documented extensive damage to marine life resulting from the heat. Between January 2023 and September 2025, 84% of the world’s coral reefs experienced bleaching-level heat stress. Over the past 30 years, nearly 5% of the ocean has seen a persistent shift in growth patterns of phytoplankton, tiny creatures that underpin food webs and regulate carbon flows. In the Antarctic, four emperor penguin colonies saw total breeding failures in 2022 during periods of record-low sea ice.

blocks.caption: Water-sprinklers spray mist to suppress dust and help curb air pollution at the BRICS summit in New Delhi, India, in September 2026. Photograph: Mukhtar Khan/AP

blocks.text: The findings were published alongside separate Copernicus research that found this year’s deadly cocktail of extreme heat and dirty air subjected more than one-third of humanity to dangerous levels of ground-level ozone pollution.

The phenomenon, known as the “ozone-climate penalty”, is the result of chemical changes that occur when certain pollutants are exposed to heat and sunlight. In the first eight months of 2026, the report found, just 5% of the world’s population has been exposed to “good” levels of ozone that fall within the World Health Organization’s guidelines.
Florian Pappenberger, director-general of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which conducted the analysis, said the findings show that “air pollution knows no border”.

“Wildfire smoke, ozone and dust can travel thousands of kilometres, affecting communities far from their source,” he said. “As the international community prepares for Cop31, these findings are a timely reminder that climate change, air quality and public health are deeply interconnected challenges that require coordinated global action.”

articles.title: Menopause supplements costing more than £400 a year ‘no better than cheap multivitamin’
articles.summary:
Many products aimed at women over 45 lack meaningful quantities of key nutrients, consumer watchdog Which? found

Menopause supplements costing more than £400 a year are no better than a…
articles.byline: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent

blocks.text: Menopause supplements costing more than £400 a year are no better than a £22-a-year multivitamin, according to analysis by the consumer watchdog Which?.

Which? found that many popular supplements that are aimed at women over 45 going through menopause or perimenopause lack meaningful quantities of key nutrients, yet cost 20 times more than standard multivitamins.

The global menopause supplement market is valued at nearly $17bn and is expected to reach $25bn by 2030, as women look for ways to manage a variety of symptoms associated with menopause such as hot flushes, poor sleep and mood swings.
But research by Which? found that none of the supplements it studied contained the correct nutrients in the right doses to support their use for menopause.

Shefalee Loth, a public health nutritionist at Which? who co-led the research, said: “Which? is concerned that the supplements industry has become a wild west and regulators are not doing enough to get a grip on dubious marketing and unchecked quasi-medical claims from firms apparently seeking to cash in on people’s health anxiety and insecurities.”

Calcium and vitamin D are the most important nutrients during perimenopause and menopause as they support bone health as oestrogen levels decline. Maintaining good levels of iron, magnesium and other vitamins and minerals can also help with symptoms.

Nutritionists from Which? examined the active ingredients in 26 popular supplements sold by retailers such as Holland & Barrett, Boots and Amazon and found that a high-quality multivitamin alongside targeted supplements where needed was often cheaper and potentially more effective than a so-called all-in-one menopause blend.

It found that Asda’s A-Z Multivitamins & Minerals, costing 6p a day (£22 a year), contained all essential vitamins plus 200mg of calcium and 100mg of magnesium. In contrast, the most expensive supplement, Love Mushrooms’ Empower, cost £1.33 a day for a two-tablet dose (£485 a year) yet did not contain menopause-specific nutrients such as magnesium and calcium.

Similarly, Wild Nutrition’s Women’s 45+ Daily Multi Nutrient, costing £1.27 a day (£468 a year), contained just 1.5µg of vitamin D, 60mg of calcium and 30mg of magnesium, significantly under NHS recommended daily amounts, Which? found.
The watchdog also found that many menopause supplements’ key nutrients were in doses too low to be beneficial, or they omitted important vitamins and minerals altogether.
The highest-scoring menopause supplement analysed, Vitabiotics’ Menopace Max, cost 93p a day (£340 a year) – more than 15 times the price of Asda’s 6p multivitamin.

The findings follow research by UCL into 201 supplements sold in the UK that found less than half of products contained vitamin D and calcium and the majority of ingredients were not specifically recommended by major menopause societies.

Responding to Which?’s research, Dr Xand van Tulleken, an honorary associate professor at the UCL Institute for Global Health, said: “Every year our annual spending on menopause supplements is hundreds of times more than our spending on menopause research. There is no persuasive evidence that menopause supplements have a significant effect on women’s symptoms, some of them are dangerous, and the pricing and marketing is exploitative and confusing. They are a massive rip-off for consumers who desperately want to be well.”

Martin Last, the director general of the Health Food Manufacturers’ Association, said: “We encourage industry manufacturers to formulate and recommend supplements as required by the many food regulations that apply to food supplements. Many life stages, including the menopause, may create increased nutritional demands on an individual and these may be met by supplementation as an addition to a healthy diet.”

articles.title: Approval of biggest coal project in NSW planning commission’s history described as ‘infamous betrayal’
articles.summary: Independent Planning Commission says climate change impacts from Hunter Valley project will be ‘outweighed’ by economic benefits
articles.byline: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent

blocks.text: The New South Wales independent planner has approved the biggest coalmine project to ever go before it, allowing mining to continue until 2045 at a Hunter Valley project described by climate groups as a “carbon bomb”.

The Independent Planning Commission (IPC) has greenlit the Hunter Valley Operations (HVO) Continuation Project after a contentious assessment that drew in climate and environment groups, unions, state authorities and more than 10,000 public submissions.

On Wednesday, the commission said the greenhouse gas emissions from the mine, near Singleton, would “contribute to climate change impacts on the people, economy and environment of the Hunter region, NSW and globally”.

But these impacts had been “outweighed by its benefits to the Hunter region and NSW, including continued employment, economic activity, support for local business, ongoing royalties and taxation revenue”.

The IPC said the decision would “provide economic stability for the Hunter region and support a more orderly transition for workers, businesses and communities as the coal industry changes over time”.

In response, Georgina Woods, the co-national coordinator of the Lock the Gate Alliance, said: “There is no other way to describe this other than a catastrophic failure of the New South Wales planning system to protect the people of the state from the worst impacts of global warming.”
Climate campaigners had strongly opposed the project, saying it was out of line with Australia’s commitments under the Paris climate agreement and could affect extreme weather events.
Groups reacted with dismay at the approval, with Rising Tide describing it as the “largest climate policy failure in NSW history”.

The Climate Council had described the project as a “climate bomb that would supercharge climate disasters”. One of its councillors – the former NSW Fire and Rescue commissioner Greg Mullins – on Wednesday raised concerns over overseas emissions from the coal.
“What NSW exports as coal, we import back as bushfires, floods, heatwaves and droughts,” Mullins said. “Climate harm does not stop at the border, and neither does the responsibility for it.”
Woods said the process for considering fossil fuel projects in NSW was “the best in the country” – including with its climate change act and an independent and transparent planning authority.
“The law was in place, and I am frankly shocked. It will go down in history as an infamous betrayal of the public trust.”
Glencore and Yancoal – the joint owners of HVO – want to continue digging coal at the north mine site until 2045, and mine from 2030 to 2042 at the south mine.

The IPC said HVO would have to prepare a plan to manage the emissions from burning the coal overseas that would limit exports to “jurisdictions with greenhouse gas emissions policies consistent with the goals of the Paris Agreement”.
The project also requires federal environmental approval – a process expected to be decided before the end of the year.
HVO said coal had been mined at the site for 75 years and the project, which it said had strong local support, provided jobs for 1,500 people.
after newsletter promotion
The state’s independent Net Zero Commission had warned the planning commission that approving the project could affect the state’s ability to meet climate targets in the future.
Over the life of the project, the company has estimated that 809m tonnes of CO2-equivalent will be released into the atmosphere.
About 794Mt of that will be emitted when the coal is burned overseas, 87% of which will come from power plants, according to presentations HVO made to the IPC.

The Net Zero Commission recommended the planning authority should consider all of the impacts from the mine’s greenhouse gases, including from the burning of the coal in power stations overseas, and pointed to advances in climate science that can attribute real-world impacts to fossil fuel projects.

A new tool released by climate scientists this week suggested the additional global heating caused by the project’s approval would expose almost half a million people to unprecedented heat, kill nearly 15 million coral colonies on the Great Barrier Reef every time it bleaches and lead to more than 100 additional deaths from heatwaves in Europe to the end of this century.

The NSW Nature Conservation Council’s chief executive, Jacqui Mumford, said the decision was Chris Minns’ “biggest climate failure” as premier and highlighted the government’s “complete inability to appropriately respond to the ever-growing climate crisis”.
The NSW state Greens MP Sue Higginson said the approval was an “absolute betrayal of the science”, saying she “wouldn’t be surprised if the decision is challenged in the courts”.
HVO said the approval “marked a pivotal milestone for 1,500 mine workers, their families and the regional economy”.
It said the company was engaging with the national environmental protection agency to secure federal approval “by the end of December 2026 to continue operations”.

The NSW Minerals Council urged the state government to pass legislation to limit the opportunity for a “legal challenge from climate activists determined to object to every coal mining approval on ideological grounds”.

articles.title: With less than 3 weeks before Alberta's referendum, Poilievre makes case for Canadian unity in Edmonton
articles.summary: Conservative Party of Canada Leader Pierre Poilievre says he supports a united Canada.

image.caption: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre delivers a speech on national unity in Edmonton on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. (John Ulan/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Edmonton·New
Conservative Party of Canada Leader Pierre Poilievre says he supports a united Canada.
Alberta's fall referendum will have question about separation

As Albertans prepare to vote in a referendum next month that will ask if the province should stay in Canada or hold a binding referendum on independence, federal Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre told an Edmonton crowd he supports a united Canada.
Poilievre addressed a crowd of over 100 people who gathered to hear him speak at a hotel in the downtown core on Tuesday evening.
The walls of the conference room where Poilievre spoke were adorned by Alberta flags and Canadian flags and some audience members were holding Canadian flags.
Tuesday's event was part of the Conservatives for Canada campaign which is seeing federal conservative politicians advocate for Confederation.
Poilievre, who grew up in Calgary, said that after speaking with some Alberta separatists, he has come to believe their problem isn’t with Canada, but with Canada's federal Liberal government.
“It is the government policies that are actually inconsistent with how Canada was meant to work in the first place,” he said in his nearly 30-minute speech.

items: Poilievre says those who vote for Alberta separation 'are not our enemies'

blocks.text: Poilievre pointed to grievances that he believes Albertans and people in several other provinces have with the current federal government like the introduction of the federal gun buyback program, the ongoing high cost of living and concerns about untapped potential in the oil and gas industry.
“Many Albertans are legitimately frustrated that a costly and controlling, big and bossy government has gone far beyond its jurisdictional boundaries in Ottawa,” he said.
“It's blocked our provinces and people from enjoying the Canadian promise.”
Poilievre said he believes separating from Canada won’t improve Alberta’s circumstances.
“Confederation made the promise to marry the massive powers of our resources in the west with the manufacturing might of the east,” he said.
“It married the autonomy of local provinces with pan-Canadian defence, trade, population and land mass. And it worked because governments did their job but stayed out of the way.”
Poilievre ended his speech by directly addressing young Albertans and Quebecers, asking them to stay united and to “double down on the Canadian promise.”

Several Conservative lawmakers who represent Alberta ridings attended Tuesday night's event, including Edmonton West MP Kelly McCauley, Leduc-Wetaskiwin MP Mike Lake and Fort McMurray-Cold Lake MP Laila Goodridge.
Parkland MP Dane Lloyd, who is the Conservatives' caucus lead on the party's campaign to stay in Canada, introduced Poilievre to the crowd.
"We love our country," he said. "We love our home province of Alberta. And that's why we are fighting for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada."
Poilievre has previously said all federal Conservative MPs will be campaigning for Canadian unity in Alberta.
Poilievre delivered his speech on Tuesday with less than three weeks to go before Albertans will vote on 10 questions in the Oct. 19 referendum.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Emma Zhao is a reporter with CBC Edmonton. You can reach her at emma.zhao@cbc.ca.

articles.title: OpenAI takes on Meta with dots agent in autonomous AI push
articles.summary: OpenAI's dots agents aim to capitalize on growing demand for agents that can handle everyday work with little supervision

blocks.text: OPENAI. OpenAI logo is seen in this illustration taken June 11, 2026
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
OpenAI's dots agents aim to capitalize on growing demand for agents that can handle everyday work with little supervision

items: OpenAI launched 'dots', always-on AI agents designed to autonomously assist users across applications, marking a significant move into the enterprise market and increasing competition with Meta.
Despite the potential of dots to enhance productivity, OpenAI faces scrutiny over safety concerns due to past incidents involving rogue AI agents, leading to a cautious approach in their deployment.
The company emphasized data privacy and safety measures, allowing users to set custom rules for the agents, while also reporting significant growth in user engagement across its AI platforms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

SAN FRANCISCO, USA – OpenAI on Tuesday, September 29, unveiled always-on agents called dots that chase user goals across apps on their own, deepening its push into the lucrative enterprise market and pitting it against Meta in the race to sell AI that can work autonomously.
The dots agents aim to capitalize on growing demand for agents that can handle everyday work with little supervision.

The launch marks a new front in the competition among AI companies to move beyond chatbots and sell software that acts on users’ behalf — a shift that could reshape how businesses operate but that has raised safety concerns after a string of incidents in which AI agents acted in ways their makers did not intend.

OpenAI has faced scrutiny after its rogue AI agents hacked Hugging Face and an Australian government health website, fanning fears about its ability to contain technology that some researchers say could kill all humans.
The company on Monday decided not to release a more powerful version of its Astra model because it showed a high willingness to mislead users about its actions.
CEO Sam Altman said dots has been “safety tested” and was powered by its model that most closely follows human directions, GPT-6 Astra.

Interest in AI agents has surged since Meta’s Muse drew millions of downloads earlier this month and jolted shares of companies that investors believe could benefit or be disrupted by autonomous services. Instinct, the startup behind the eponymous agent, also quadrupled its valuation to $10 billion this week, a little over a month after its previous funding round.

OpenAI launched dots at its annual Developer Day in San Francisco on Tuesday while also touting its growing business and consumer presence, a sign that the reception for the company’s Astra model has allowed it to make up ground in the AI race.

Growing quickly is crucial for OpenAI’s plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on AI data centers and keep pace with rivals such as Anthropic and Meta. The company, which ignited the AI boom with ChatGPT in late 2022, is also preparing for an IPO that could value it at more than $1 trillion. Rival Anthropic could be worth $2 trillion when it goes public.

“We believe (the agent) is going to feel like a whole new way to work with AI. This is the real deal version of AI that we’ve always imagined for ourselves,” Altman said at the event, which had around 2,500 in-person attendees.

OpenAI’s live demos to show off the new capabilities, however, hit snags as the agents repeatedly failed to deliver voice updates in response to requests. “We might have some voice difficulties at the moment. Which is pretty unfortunate,” Developer Experience chief Romain Huet said on stage after a command failed.
One OpenAI employee said on X that the glitches stemmed from rolling out all the updates at once, but that OpenAI remained committed to live demos.

Dots can manage projects as they evolve, such as updating a sales proposal when customer needs change, and building a working demo for review. Users can communicate with dots on Slack and Teams, and the agents can draw on OpenAI’s Codex and ChatGPT Work tools to research, analyze data, prepare documents and build software.

On Tuesday, OpenAI highlighted safeguards it has built into dots. It said users could set custom rules that dictate what dots can do and when the agents should seek permission, adding that sensitive tasks such as changing passwords and permanently deleting data require explicit user consent.
The company also said dots run on their own cloud computers, and that it was rolling out private intelligence tools to check for safety risks without retaining business customers’ data.

Several tech executives, including Palantir CEO Alex Karp, have in recent months said that businesses need certainty that AI companies are not retaining their data, especially in regulated industries such as healthcare and finance.

Reuters reported on Friday that OpenAI was still working to understand the full scope of its rogue agent activity, two months after the Hugging Face hack, with the latest example coming when the company said its agents had leaked 53 images from ChatGPT users.

OpenAI reiterated on Tuesday that it does not use business customers’ data to train its AI by default, and that personal-plan users could opt out of sharing conversations and dots work used for training.

Weekly users of Codex and ChatGPT Work have reached more than 35 million, up from about 5 million Codex users in June, the company said Tuesday, while consumer-focused ChatGPT now has over 1.2 billion weekly users.

The company is rolling out ChatGPT Space, which is a shared workspace for business teams and its AI agents, as well as the cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol model and a $500 Pro plan offering higher usage and faster performance. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Alan Cayetano says Lacson acts as chief justice, prosecutor; Ping fires back
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has criticized Sen. Ping Lacson for acting like a chief justice, prosecutor, and more, saying the latter dictated how the flood control probes should go.…

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 1:41pm

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has criticized Sen. Ping Lacson for acting like a chief justice, prosecutor, and more, saying the latter dictated how the flood control probes should go. Lacson fired back by questioning Cayetano’s credibility.
In an ongoing verbal war between the two senators that has been ongoing since July, Cayetano accused Lacson of acting like he held authority over the investigation.

"Si Senator Lacson kasi ay Chief Justice Lacson, Prosecutor Lacson, DOJ (Department of Justice) Lacson, Persecutor Lacson, siya na lahat, Secretary Lacson – siya na ang lahat. Siya na ang nagdidikta eh – sa LLDA (Laguna Lake Development Authority), Blue Ribbon Committee, DILG (Department of Interior and Local Government), at PRA (Philippine Reclamation Authority). Kahit sila na mismo ang magsabi, babaguhin niya," Cayetano said in a Facebook livestream.

(Senator Lacson is also Chief Justice Lacson, Prosecutor Lacson, DOJ Lacson, Persecutor Lacson, he is everything, Secretary Lacson—he is everything. He is dictating everything to the LLDA, the Blue Ribbon Committee, DILG, and PRA. Even if they are the one who said it, he would change it.)

The statement came days after the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon confirmed to Cayetano during a Senate budget hearing that there were no ghost projects in Taguig City.

However, Lacson, who said that there was evidence of anomalous projects in Taguig City, told Dizon not to contradict his agency’s own findings. In a previous media interview, Lacson said that Dizon called him after the budget hearing, apologizing and expressing that he felt set up by the question.
On Wednesday, Lacson shrugged off Cayetano’s latest insult.
“If it were coming from someone credible, I’d take it as a compliment,” he said on X.

Dizon, who found himself between the two senators’ feud, clarified that his statement must be taken within the context of the question. He only said that while there were no conclusive ghost projects to be found in Taguig City yet, investigation is still ongoing. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: NFA: Full warehouses limited 2025 palay purchases
articles.summary: The National Food Authority (NFA) on Wednesday explained that it was unable to fully utilize its 2025 budget for palay (unhusked rice) procurement because its warehouses were already full.

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 1:40pm
The National Food Authority (NFA) on Wednesday explained that it was unable to fully utilize its 2025 budget for palay (unhusked rice) procurement because its warehouses were already full.

The NFA made the statement after state auditors flagged the agency for falling short of its statutory buffer stock requirement, with 408,944 metric tons (MT) of rice in stock, equivalent to just 10.68 days of supply instead of the 15 days mandated under the amended Rice Tariffication Law (RTL).
The shortfall supposedly stemmed from procurement challenges in 2025, when the NFA met only 77% of its 545,000-MT purchasing target.
The Commission on Audit (COA) earlier raised concerns over the NFA's rice buffer stock and procurement performance.

According to NFA administrator Larry Lacson, the agency's 2025 buffer stock target remained at nine days because the amended RTL, which increased the requirement, was approved only after the agency's 2025 budget had already been finalized.

"First, the amended RTL was approved in December 2024. Before that, our mandated buffer stock was only nine days. By December 2024, the 2025 program and budget had already been finalized," Lacson said in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.

"Our target for 2025 was still nine days because the change did not make it into the budget cycle. So for 2025, our target remained at nine days. In total, we achieved that—it was even more than 10 days," he added.
The NFA also said it had been aggressive in purchasing palay in 2024, leaving little to no space in its warehouses in 2025.

"Second, even if we wanted to spend all the funds allocated for procurement, our warehouses were full—completely full—because we were aggressive in 2024, buying more and more. Our buffer stock reached almost 13 days, which is why our warehouses were full in 2025," Lacson said.
The NFA had reportedly been allocated P14 billion in subsidies from 2024 to 2025 but was able to utilize only around P10 billion of this amount for palay procurement.

Lacson said the NFA had a total of P17 billion in funds available in 2024, including P8 billion carried over from the previous year. It spent P12 billion that year, leaving more than P4 billion for 2025.

"That's why in 2025, we were able to purchase a little over P10 billion worth of palay. That's still higher than the P9 billion annual budget provided for the year. We have to take into account that we were also using excess funds from 2023," he added.
As of September 18, the NFA projected its milled-rice stock at 278,444 MT, covering roughly seven days of national demand.

Between January and September 2026, the NFA bought 92,032 MT of palay at P27 to P30 per kilo and disbursed 207,648 MT of rice overall, including 126,737 MT allocated to its P20-per-kilo rice program and 28,983 MT in total releases.
Meanwhile, the Department of Agriculture said a competitive auction of 39,597 MT of older rice generated roughly P1.1 billion and freed up storage space for newly harvested palay.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Coalition launches online signature campaign for anti-political dynasty law
articles.summary: The Dapat Isa Lang Coalition on Wednesday launched its online platform for its signature campaign to enact a genuine anti-political dynasty law.

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 1:33pm
The Dapat Isa Lang Coalition on Wednesday launched its online platform for its signature campaign to enact a genuine anti-political dynasty law.

The coalition seeks to prohibit political dynasties up to the 4th civil degree of consanguinity, allowing only one member of a family to hold a national elective office and only one to hold a local elective office at a time.
Interested individuals may visit the d1l.org to sign, according to the coalition.

“Why the 4th degree? Because we know the Filipino family. Hindi natapos ang pamilya sa asawa at anak. Hindi natatapos ito sa magulang at kapatid. Kasama sa tunay na operasyon ng isang political clan ang tiyuhin, tiyahin, the rest of the family, pamangkin, pinsan, and sometimes even common-law partners,” lawyer Eirene Aguila said.

(Why the 4th degree? Because we know the Filipino family. The family does not end with the spouse and children. It does not end with the parents and siblings. The real operation of a political clan includes uncles, aunts, the rest of the family, nieces and nephews, cousins, and sometimes even common-law partners.)
Dapat Isa Lang was launched as a signature campaign in May this year aiming to gather at least seven million signatures or 10 percent of the country's registered voters.
The Supreme Court has recently directed Congress to enact an anti-political dynasty law at the earliest opportunity, saying its failure to do so for 39 years constitutes grave abuse of discretion.
The SC, however, is leaving it to Congress to define what constitutes a political dynasty and determine the scope of the prohibition.

Following this, retired Associate Justice Antonio Carpio said they will seek recourse from the SC should Congress pass the controversial anti-political dynasty bill principally authored by Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III and House Majority Leader Ferdinand Alexander “Sandro” Marcos.
The bill, passed on third and final reading in June, bans relatives up to the second degree of consanguinity or affinity from running for or occupying a post in the same constituency or jurisdiction.
For his part, Marcos said that the bill is not yet set in stone as revisions can still be made during the deliberations of the bicameral conference committee. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: DENR seeks binding global plastics treaty to address plastic crisis
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has called for a unified global framework to address the plastic problem worldwide.

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 1:30pm
The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has called for a unified global framework to address the plastic problem worldwide.
Environment Undersecretary for Finance Analiza Teh said unified global policies help reduce financial risks for investors.

She adds that standardizing Extended Producer Responsibility metrics and regulatory terms lowers cross-border compliance expenses, providing institutional investors and multilateral development banks the regulatory certainty needed to fund large-scale sustainable infrastructure and public-private partnerships.

"We cannot solve the climate crisis without solving the plastic crisis. A future Global Plastics Treaty would be the most critical environmental deal since the 2015 Paris Agreement," said Teh during the High-Level Business and Policy Roundtable on the Global Plastics Treaty in New York, USA.
"To achieve our 2040 goal of ending plastic pollution, the final treaty must establish a predictable, standardized framework that aligns global capital with circular outcomes," she added.

Teh called on private companies to become active partners by sharing data on alternative materials, supporting mandatory rules to counter artificially cheap virgin plastics, and directly funding regional waste management infrastructure.
"A weak treaty is one that focuses only on waste management and recycling. This will lock countries into a permanent cycle of toxic exposure and waste management expenses it cannot afford,” said Teh.
In the Philippines, the DENR has issued 155 show cause letters to companies over alleged failure to recycle their plastic waste in compliance with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Law.

In 2024, the Palace said that audited recovery rates reached 59.98% for rigid plastics and 56.33% for flexible plastics, which is higher than the target of 40%. It added that the target for 2026 is 60%. — LA, GMA News

articles.title: Double beds, aircon and big-screen TVs: Indonesia suspends officials over luxury prison cells
articles.summary:
Indonesia’s prisons have long faced allegations that well-connected inmates can obtain preferential treatment through bribery

Five Indonesian prison officials have been suspended after…

blocks.text: Five Indonesian prison officials have been suspended after investigators found an apartment-style compound complete with airconditioners, big-screen televisions and expensive cars allegedly used by inmates at a prison near Jakarta.

“We found strong indications that certain prisoners had access to special facilities unavailable to ordinary prisoners,” said Syafrida Rachmawati Rasahan, a member of Indonesia’s ombudsman, on Tuesday. “We encountered prisoners inside the residential compound and discovered facilities resembling home stays, apartments and villas rather than prison housing.”

blocks.caption: Indonesia’s ombudsman discovered facilities resembling home stays rather than prison cells. Photograph: Ombudsman Republik Indonesia/Facebook

blocks.text: Investigators also reported finding sofas and dining areas in the units, and a gym and golf simulator under construction in the complex.

The incident has drawn widespread public attention and renewed scrutiny of Indonesia’s prisons, which have long faced allegations that wealthy or well-connected prisoners can obtain preferential treatment through bribery.

The allegations centre on Cibinong prison in Bogor, near Jakarta, where investigators from the ombudsman found more than 10 residential units separate from regular prison cells during a surprise inspection on 23 September, Rasahan said.
Rudi Setiawan, inspector general of the ministry of immigration and corrections, said dozens of prisoners and prison employees had been questioned as part of the inquiry.
“We have suspended five structural officials, including the Cibinong prison chief, who are suspected of being responsible for the incident uncovered by the ombudsman,” Setiawan said.

The four-hectare (10-acre) Cibinong prison houses a mix of prisoners, including those convicted of corruption and other high-profile prisoners. The identities of prisoners allegedly living in the compound have not been officially disclosed.

blocks.caption: Dozens of prisoners and prison employees have been questioned as part of the inquiry. Photograph: Ombudsman Republik Indonesia/Facebook

blocks.text: Lawmakers, anti-corruption activists and watchdog groups have urged authorities to identify which prisoners occupied the facilities and whether prison officials accepted payments in exchange for the privileges.

The buildings were originally intended as official housing for prison personnel, but investigators are examining whether they were converted into unauthorised accommodation for prisoners, said Setiawan.

The case is the latest embarrassment for the corrections system in Indonesia, which has struggled for years with overcrowding, corruption and repeated allegations that affluent prisoners can buy privileges unavailable to the broader prison population.

articles.title: NSW man accused of murdering neighbour – and then murdering his relative two weeks later
articles.summary: Police allege Nicholas Scott killed 79-year-old then ‘set upon’ 59-year-old relative who arrived at Gurranang to sort out estate

blocks.text: A man accused of murdering two members of a family on the same property a fortnight apart has faced court.
The body of a 59-year-old man was found by police on Monday afternoon in a shed on a property at Gurranang, about 25km north of Grafton in northern New South Wales.
The discovery was made as police combed the address for clues two weeks after a 79-year-old man’s body was found inside a home on the property.
Det Supt Joe Doueihi on Wednesday said the alleged murder victims were related, adding the younger man came to NSW to help police with their investigation and to sort out the 79-year-old’s estate.
He alleged the 59-year-old was “set upon” by a neighbour when he went to his deceased relative’s property.
“It’s absolutely shocking for that family and for that community,” the homicide squad commander told reporters.
Police alleged the neighbour – 32-year-old Nicholas Scott – was responsible for both murders.
Scott was arrested at a hospital in Grafton, where he was receiving treatment, at about midday on Tuesday.
He was taken to Grafton police station where he was charged with two counts of murder and stealing a motor vehicle.
Scott briefly appeared in court on Wednesday morning and did not apply for bail.
He will remain behind bars before returning to court in December.
Supt Joanne Schultz told reporters on Tuesday the scene was extremely confronting and traumatic for first responders.
after newsletter promotion
“[Police] had attended the property to make further inquiries, they did not anticipate what they found,” she said.
Police believe the 59-year-old man died in the past 24 to 48 hours, two weeks after police first came to the rural acreage to investigate the older man’s death.
“The scene was not maintained for the entirety of that time,” Supt Schultz said.
The deceased men appeared to have suffered similar injuries.
Strike Force Faneel continues to investigate the deaths.

articles.summary: Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. Israel’s military says it has no record of the attack.

blocks.text: Six-year-old Raseel al-Balawi in Gaza has had more than 20 surgeries since an Israeli air strike injured her in late July.
Witnesses say her tent in al-Mawasi camp was hit by a strike from an Israeli helicopter, and she now has to have frequent surgeries to try and control infections in her wounds.
Israel's military says it has no record of the attack and that it "regrets any harm to civilians".
BBC Eye Investigations has spent time with Raseel across the summer, as the ceasefire falters and bombardment continues, to see the challenges doctors are facing in Gaza.

The BBC World Service has been filming across the summer in Gaza to reveal how children there are coping amid the near-total destruction of the infrastructure they rely on to survive. You can watch the full film on iPlayer.

articles.title: 'Backpack' declared Alaska's Fat Bear Week winner
articles.summary: "Backpack" defeated a bear known only as "910" in the final round of the annual competition.

blocks.text: A brown bear known as 89 Backpack has won the annual Fat Bear Week competition, after what the US National Parks Service described as a "battle of size, skill, snack acquisition, and strategic loafing".
Backpack's wideness narrowly defeated a bear known only as 910, earning 103,344 votes to 910's 98,253 in the final round of the competition, which is run by the Katmai National Park in Alaska.
The National Parks Service thanked the 16 bears who "involuntarily participated" in the competition, now in its thirteenth year.
Backpack, who was described by one supporter as having both the "chonk and the badonk", will shortly enter hibernation, which can last up to six months.

His mother Holly was the 2019 Fat Bear Week winner. Backpack's name derives not from what another supporter described as the "light bulb shape" of his body, but his habit, as a cub, of climbing onto Holly's back when she waded through the park's salmon-filled Brooks River.
Another supporter described him as being a "big fuzzy boy".

But Backpack was not without his detractors. One person said she felt that Bear 910, a female who raised both her biological cub and an adopted niece, was a "larger bear all around. Backpack just has a bigger booty".
"I just feel like 910 really put in the work this year," another 910 fan wrote on the park's Facebook page, while a voter commented, "She round, she thick my girl 910 got my vote."

articles.title: Reanimated AI Greta Garbo stars again … in a ball-bearing advert
articles.summary:
Relatives of Hollywood legend say her doppelganger could now be used for more glamorous roles

She shimmered in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies – now Greta Garbo may…

blocks.text: She shimmered in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies – now Greta Garbo may be about to star in cinema’s new AI age.

More than a century after her screen debut and decades after her ashes were laid to rest in a Swedish woodland cemetery, the Hollywood superstar’s descendants are ready to consider an AI version of her taking a 21st-century film role.

Her likeness has already been reanimated for an advert for a Swedish industrial company, using AI generation technology. The practice some critics call “ghostploitation” has also been used in the case of the actor Val Kilmer, who died last year.

Asked if the AI Garbo could be cast in other roles, Craig Reisfield, one of three relatives who manage her legacy, told the Guardian: “I won’t say no, especially having seen what I’ve seen. It’s pretty incredible and lifelike. So what’s to say that you can’t bring Greta Garbo back in some kind of fashion in a film role?”

Reisfield said he was “flabbergasted” when he saw the AI version of his great-aunt created for publicity for the ball-bearings giant SKF. The connection comes because Garbo’s second-ever screen role was in a 1921 promotional film involving the Gothenburg-based company.

While Garbo was the definition of glamour in Hollywood’s golden age, appearing as a famous ballerina in Grand Hotel (1932) and as a doomed courtesan in Camille (1936), the 99-second AI performance for SKF is intercut with shots of ball-bearings.
However, the quality of the AI production has prompted the possibility, at least, of a greater digital comeback.

“I was totally impressed: the mannerisms that they could capture and manipulate, her dress, facial images and even her voice,” said Reisfield, a Swedish-American who used to drive for Garbo and saw her often for family occasions when she lived in New York.
“It was startling what they could do and very impactful. And it was touching, from my perspective having known her.”

blocks.caption: Greta Garbo and John Barrymore in Grand Hotel. Her famous line ‘I want to be alone’ comes from the 1932 MGM film. Photograph: PictureLux/The Hollywood Archive/Alamy

blocks.text: A far cry from the hand-cranked cameras that captured Garbo’s early work, the SKF performance was conjured by humans prompting AI models including China’s Seedream and Google’s Nano Banana Pro.

Unusually for AI film-making, the creators did not feed moving or still images of Garbo into the AI because the material was protected by copyright. Instead, they used text prompts to create her likeness, including her ice-blue eyes and wavy blond bob. A human actor then played her role with her AI-generated appearance overlaid. Her voice was recreated from a recording from an early film.

The resulting version of Garbo appears to have gone beyond the “uncanny valley” – the problem for AI film-makers in which the closer to an actual likeness an AI rendering becomes, the more strangely implausible it seems.
after newsletter promotion

AI Garbo’s lines, however, are not perhaps quite up to the standards of those given to her by MGM studio writers. At one point, she sounds like Liz Truss complaining about the “disgrace” of Britain’s cheese imports, when she says “around 20% of all global energy is lost to friction: a terrible waste”.

Several big film studios are investing in AI startups or collaborating with new AI studios. Veteran directors including Ron Howard and Paul Schrader are working on AI-enabled films, while a new generation of AI-native film-makers such as Kavan the Kid and Gossip Goblin are using AI to build huge audiences outside the conventional studio system.

Asked whether the real Garbo would have wanted to continue performing as an AI-enabled actor, Reisfield said: “She was at the forefront of cinema in the silent film era. She made the transition to ‘talkies’ and dominated box office receipts.
“So to imagine her as an AI-enabled actor given her track record and ability to captivate and connect with audiences of both men and women isn’t inconceivable.”

Reisfield said the custodians of the rights to Garbo’s voice, name, image and publicity aimed to “preserve, protect, and enhance” her legacy and were “very discerning” on partnerships. Her likeness has been posthumously used by the fashion houses Ferragamo, Gucci and Louis Vuitton but the AI performance for SKF is her first in moving images.
Whatever the future holds for AI Garbo, it kept to the true spirit of the actor by signing off the ball-bearing advert with her immortal line from Grand Hotel: “I want to be alone.”

articles.title: Erwin Tulfo files bill seeking long-term tourism campaign for PH
articles.summary: Senator Erwin Tulfo has filed a bill seeking to establish a long-term tourism campaign to sustain gains in the country"s tourism sector.

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 12:58pm
Senator Erwin Tulfo has filed a bill seeking to establish a long-term tourism campaign to sustain gains in the country’s tourism sector.

Under Senate Bill No. 2511, or the “Philippine Tourism Campaign Slogan Act,” Tulfo wants the country’s official tourism slogan to remain in use for at least 15 years, regardless of changes in administration.

“While changes in tourism campaigns may be intended to reflect evolving priorities and strategies, the frequent introduction and replacement of slogans may also result in discontinuity in the country’s tourism identity, dilute public familiarity and require substantial resources for rebranding and implementation,” Tulfo said in the bill’s explanatory note.
The Department of Tourism (DOT) launched the country’s current tourism slogan, “Love the Philippines,” in 2023, replacing “It’s More Fun in the Philippines,” which had been used since 2012.
The senator's sister, former DOT secretary Wanda Tulfo-Teo retained the “It’s More Fun in the Philippines” slogan during her term.

However, the “Love the Philippines” campaign drew controversy over its execution after its advertising agency, DDB Philippines, used stock footage of locations outside the Philippines in its audiovisual presentation. The campaign was launched under then-Tourism Secretary Christina Frasco.
The DOT later ended its contract with the advertising agency behind the campaign as it supposedly violated the terms of its tourism branding campaign contract.
During the Senate’s deliberations on the DOT’s proposed P5.47-billion budget for 2027, Tulfo raised concerns over the frequent changes in the country’s tourism slogans.

“Unlike Malaysia, which has ‘Truly Asia.’ There are slogans like that. Soon, bet you, when another administration takes over, it won’t be ‘Love (the Philippines)’ anymore. What is going on here?” he said.
Malaysia has used “Malaysia, Truly Asia” as its tourism slogan since 1999, although the campaign has undergone changes in branding and implementation over the years.
Among the Philippines’ notable tourism slogans was “WOW Philippines,” which was used from 2002 to 2012.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: NUP decries alleged withholding of infra, social aid funds, seeks quick release
articles.summary: 'The practice of punishing districts and communities for any opinions or votes contrary to majority positions that are expressed by their representatives should be ended,' NUP says

blocks.text: CONGRESS. The House of Representatives building at the Batasang Pambansa Complex in Quezon City on September 17, 2025.
Jire Carreon/Rappler
'The practice of punishing districts and communities for any opinions or votes contrary to majority positions that are expressed by their representatives should be ended,' NUP says

items: Lawmakers from the National Unity Party (NUP) are demanding the immediate release of withheld funds from the 2025 and 2026 budget, citing financial strain on congressional districts due to unimplemented DPWH projects.

They allege that certain projects have been unfairly excluded from funding and that social assistance funds have been withheld, calling for an end to the practice of tagging projects as 'for later release.'

The NUP also criticizes political motivations behind budget delays, urging that appropriations be released upon the effectivity of the General Appropriations Act to ensure fair treatment across districts.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Lawmakers from the National Unity Party (NUP) called for the immediate release to the districts of withheld funds that are supposedly still tagged “for later release” or FLR from the 2025 and 2026 budget.

In a statement on Wednesday, September 30, the House’s second largest bloc alleged that two in every five Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) projects under the 2026 General Appropriations Act (GAA) have not been implemented, placing congressional districts under financial and operational strain.

“There appears to be an uneven and selective approach in the programming and continuation of DPWH projects across certain districts and provinces. A number of multi-year, previously prioritized DPWH flagship projects have reportedly been excluded from the National Expenditure Program (NEP), despite years of prior funding and physical execution,” the statement reads.
“In certain districts and provinces, projects that had been identified and funded were later declared non-implementable by the department’s district offices, without explanation,” it added.

Congressmen also claimed that allocated funds for social amelioration such as the Assistance for Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), and Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) of the Department of Health (DOH), have either been withheld or impounded.

“We ask for the immediate release of all AICS and MAIFIP funds allocated to the districts and sectors deprived of this assistance, including the approximately P300 million and P120 million now withheld at the central offices of DSWD and DOH,” they said.
NUP laid out numerous requests, including a call to discontinue the practice of tagging district projects as “for later release.”

“We urge that the FY 2027 GAA carry a general provision confirming that every appropriation authorized in the Act is released upon its effectivity, with the Act itself serving as the allotment release document in accordance with law and jurisprudence, and prohibiting the classification of any item as ‘for later release,’ ‘needs clearance,’ or under any similar designation not expressly provided in the Act,” the NUP said.
Lawmakers also allude to supposed delays in budget release caused by politicking.

“The practice of punishing districts and communities for any opinions or votes contrary to majority positions that are expressed by their representatives should be ended. We are, after all, a democracy,” they said.

This is not the first time NUP said something along these lines. In February, the NUP appealed to the House leadership not to go after lawmakers because of how they will vote on the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte. At the time, NUP said it was unlikely to back the complaint against her.
The NUP was publicly critical of Speaker Bojie Dy’s leadership earlier this year, and even floated the idea of jumping to the House minority.

Puno was upset with budget woes hounding congressional districts, including funds tagged for later release, and how the House leadership is representing the lower chamber in talks with the executive branch.
Rappler has reached out to Speaker Bojie Dy’s office and DPWH for comment, but they have yet to respond as of posting. – Rappler.com

articles.title: NUP flags delays, non-release of funds for infra, social programs
articles.summary: The National Unity Party, which has 58 members in the House of Representatives, on Wednesday alleged delayed fund releases for infrastructure projects and social programs funded under the 2025 and…

blocks.text: Published September 30, 2026 12:52pm

The National Unity Party (NUP), which has 58 members in the House of Representatives, on Wednesday alleged delayed fund releases for infrastructure projects and social programs funded under the 2025 and 2026 national budget.

“We are concerned about persistent reports of significant delays in the release of funds for infrastructure projects authorized under the 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Act (GAA). With approximately 40 percent of DPWH projects under the 2026 GAA reportedly still awaiting execution, these delays have placed severe financial and operational strain on affected provinces and districts,” the NUP said in a statement read by its chairman Deputy Speaker Ronaldo Puno of Antipolo.

The NUP said that there appears to be an uneven and selective approach in the programming and continuation of Department of Public Works and Highways projects across certain districts and provinces, with a number of multi-year, previously prioritized DPWH flagship projects reportedly excluded from the National Expenditure Program (NEP) despite years of prior funding and physical execution.
“In certain districts and provinces, projects that had been identified and funded were later declared non-implementable by the Department’s district offices, without explanation,” the NUP added.

“The consequence of all this is felt most by local communities because every unreleased peso drives up project costs through delay, and leads directly to unbuilt roads, unopened classrooms, and lost local jobs. We believe that everyone should ensure the adherence of the preparation and execution of the national budget to established rules and reasonable standards,” the NUP added.

Likewise, the NUP said that funds already allocated to the districts or sectors under the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations under the Department of Social Welfare an Development as well as Medical Assistance for AICS worth P300 million and Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) worth P120 million under the Department of Health have been withheld or impounded.

“AICS and MAIFIP are poverty-alleviation and social-protection lifelines for our people in dire need. It remains our firm position that the distribution and continuity of national resources, whether during initial budget preparation or final fund releases, and whether for infrastructure or for social services, should be ensured,” the NUP pointed out.

NUP said its call is in accordance with the 2025 Supreme Court decision on the PhilHealth case which declared that public funds should be allocated and released according to law and to standards fixed in advance, not according to the preferences of whoever holds the funds at a given moment.

“Withholding the districts’ appropriated projects for whatever reason, or declaring them non-implementable after they have been funded, or impounding social assistance already allocated, is the kind of discretion the Court has said the Constitution does not allow,” the NUP said.
GMA News Online asked the DPWH and DSWD for comment but they have yet to issue statements as of posting time. —KG, GMA News
